reasons: Lake identity confirms case_name Coolidge v. New Hampshire, court U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 1971-06-21, and year 1971.
Lake citations confirm official 403 U.S. 443, parallels 91 S. Ct. 2022 and 29 L. Ed. 2d 564, and vendor neutral 1971 U.S. LEXIS 25.
The opinion devotes Part II-C to the plain-view exception and holds that the exception could not justify the Pontiac seizure.
The text states the doctrine's requirements: prior justification, inadvertent discovery, and immediately apparent incriminating character.
residual_risks: Role strength is a corpus-taxonomy judgment, but the disclosed opinion supports plain view as a central home.

defect.evidence_quote: It is well established that under certain circumstances the police may seize evidence in plain view without a warrant.
defect.locator_note: content_page.md front-matter holding; group_inventory holding payload
defect.problem: The holding as framed is incomplete and overclaims an 'ORIGIN of the modern plain-view doctrine' that is not verifiable from the disclosed lake record or opinion text. The opinion itself describes warrantless plain-view seizure as already 'well established' and discusses earlier plain-view applications.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace with a complete, text-grounded holding: Stewart plurality formulated limits on plain-view seizures: plain view supplements a prior lawful intrusion, requires inadvertent discovery under Coolidge's legacy formulation, and requires the incriminating character to be immediately apparent; because police knew the car's description and location in advance and intended to seize it, plain view did not justify the seizure.

reasons: The disclosed lake record has no holdings field confirming the 'origin' characterization.
The content holding is visibly truncated after 'incriminating…', so it does not state a complete rule.
The opinion supports a narrower formulation but not the comparative claim that Coolidge is the origin of the modern doctrine.
residual_risks: If the corpus wants to keep an 'origin/modern' label, it needs disclosed secondary authority or a corpus-wide rule-source record not present here.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Avoid 'ORIGIN' unless supported by an disclosed authority; use 'Stewart plurality formulation of plain-view limits' instead.

reasons: Part I holds the Pontiac warrant invalid because it was not issued by a neutral and detached magistrate.
The opinion says the Attorney General was the chief investigator and later prosecutor, and therefore not the neutral and detached magistrate required by the Constitution.
Treatment merits are outside Lens A, but the payload matches the lake point_override for legacy-limited-coolidge-v-new-hampshire.
Lake treatment identifies Horton v. California, cluster_id 112448, cite 496 U.S. 128, with field_ii limited.
residual_risks: No independent Lens A treatment or currency audit performed.

reasons: Treatment merits are outside Lens A, but the payload tracks the lake treatment fields: field_i_validity caution, as_of_content 1971-06-21, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, composite_basis migration-seed, and the Horton scope note.
Lake treatment states that Horton abandoned inadvertence while prior-justification and immediately-apparent requirements survive.
residual_risks: No independent Lens A treatment or currency audit performed.
